I will keep things simple and steady. In Quzhou County, the crop I trust most is the usual winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits my habits, my age, and the way farming works here: it is familiar, easy to manage with common machines, easy to sell, and less risky than trying something fancy. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops, because that makes labor, fertilizer, irrigation, and pest control harder to manage. So I will plant improved winter wheat on all my land, harvest it in early summer, and then plant hybrid summer maize right after. I will use moderate fertilizer, not too much, because I want stable yield and controlled cost. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat here usually needs more water at key stages. I will do rotary tillage because it is practical and cheaper for me than deep ploughing every season. I will spray only as needed, but in my plan I will count the usual number of applications for weeds, disease, and insects. I am choosing the plain, dependable path because I care most about stable output and manageable work.
